claims.text: The material under study is solidified FeNiCrMn alloy.
The dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn is governed by thermally activated dislocation glide.
Thermally activated dislocation glide controls the strength of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes.
Thermally activated dislocation glide controls the ductility of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes.
Temperature and strain rate are the controlled interventions.
Dislocation density and arrangement are the proposed structural mediators.
The strength of FeNiCrMn will vary with temperature and strain rate according to a thermally activated process.
The ductility of FeNiCrMn will vary with temperature and strain rate according to a thermally activated process.
Room temperature and a quasi-static strain rate define the baseline condition.
The proposed applicability range is -200°C to 600°C.
The proposed applicability range is 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
The activation energy and its dependence on temperature and strain rate are unknown.
The hypothesis can be tested using uniaxial tensile tests over multiple temperatures and strain rates while measuring dislocation density and arrangement by electron microscopy.
Failure of strength and ductility to follow a thermally activated process would falsify the hypothesis.
Failure of dislocation density and arrangement to correlate with dynamic behavior would falsify the hypothesis.
